title: How the build's sessions are organized: a coordinator per repo
why: Orchestrator, Oct 28 14:58 CDT: you proposed three tiers (coordinator, lane leads, triage, all Opus); an Opus blind review with web research says the shape is sound but the cut is wrong.
note: Rulings by shiv, Oct 28 (chat; full text in docs/decisions/session-tiers.md, L0): 14:59: one coordinator per repo; coordinators may message each other to share a resource (a simulator, a loaded machine) and may touch other repos, but mainly run their own repo's lanes; claude-settings touches every repo a little. 15:01: no coded guard or file-ownership record for clashing lanes (a good brief and merging overlapping edits are enough); his want is better file splitting, no lane filed yet; false done is already covered by merge.py and rule verification-verify-against-repo. 15:03: triage is always a standing session, and each coordinator spawns it first, before any lane session. 15:04: revise the solo-versus-orchestrate rules to match the tiers; he wants an Opus review and is open to being interviewed. 15:11 ("B for sure actually"): a third standing role, the batch runner. It owns the integration batch, the CI waits, the merge tool runs and archiving lanes, so the coordinator holds only lane state and talks with him. 15:12: when he names the wrong tier or brings work to the wrong session, that session pushes back in one line (its tier, the right one, why), then still handles or routes it; into session-tiers.md, and lane L1 puts it in the output style or rules. Opus planner proposes lanes L1 (rules, glossary), L2 (skills), L3 (session-start guard); three owner questions asked in chat, to the page after 5 minutes (c202). Open: waiting-page item 50 (lane sessions Sonnet or Opus, pick a recommended); whether he answers triage directly more often, to save both sessions' context; a per-tier context limit (Oct 28 15:08: can Opus 5.5 orchestrators have a different limit than the coordinator; docs research pending, item to follow). Placed after c200 (triage 12, Oct 28).
